The earnings decline was partly attributed to costs associated with the commencement and ramp up of Resorts World New York City’s (RWNYC) full commercial casino operations, higher depreciation and higher financing costs for the development of the integrated resort.
The earnings drop was also due to an RM18.1 million unrealised forex translation loss on its US dollar-denominated borrowings during the quarter compared with a RM184.6 million translation gain a year earlier.
However, GENM’s Q2 revenue jumped 32% to RM3.85 billion from RM2.92 billion a year earlier, mainly due to contributions from the commencement of commercial casino operations at RWNYC.
The New York resort launched its full casino operations with 242 table games and 2,500 slot machines in April, with another 1,400 slot machines added subsequently.
For the first half of FY2026, net profit plunged 91% to RM43.6 million from RM489.3 million while revenue rose 22% to RM6.72 billion from RM5.51 billion.
In a note today, Public Investment Bank (PublicInvest) said GENM’s topline was lifted by contributions from RWNYC but its bottomline was dragged down by higher costs.
“While we had anticipated the new casino operations in New York to incur higher operating costs at the initial stage, the scale of losses came in larger than expected.
“Despite our projection of an improving earnings trajectory, visibility remains weak at this juncture given the uncertainty surrounding the health of the US economy,” it said.
PublicInvest said while the New York casino expansion may be seen as a catalyst, it is not likely to be earnings accretive in the next one to two years given its hefty project cost of US$5.5 billion (RM22.2 billion).
The bank cut its FY2026-2028F earnings forecasts by an average of 11%, and kept its “hold” call while lowering its target price to RM1.88 from RM2.14 previously.
TA Research noted that GENM’s US operations chalked up a 120.9% growth in revenue to RM1.5 billion in Q2, thanks to the commercialisation of casino operations at RWNYC.
This means that the US business is catching up to the RM1.8 billion quarterly revenue contribution from the Malaysia operations, it added.
The research house upgraded its recommendation to “hold” from “sell” after the stock’s recent correction, with a target price of RM1.82 per share.
GENM closed one sen or 0.6% lower at RM1.72, giving it a market capitalisation of RM10.21 billion. The stock has fallen 16% year to date.
Lim Kok Thay – the son of Genting founder Lim Goh Tong – and his son Keong Hui, have a deemed interest of 73.85% in GENM as at March 16, 2026, according to its 2025 annual report.

title: Genting Malaysia reports strong Q2 revenue growth
author: Focus Gaming News Editorial Team
body:
Genting Malaysia reports strong Q2 revenue growth
The company reported a 32 per cent year-on-year increase in second-quarter revenue.
Malaysia.- Genting Malaysia has reported a net profit of MYR27m (US$6.7m) for the second quarter of 2026, an improvement over a net loss of MYR25.2m (US$6.4m) in the first quarter of 2026. Group-wide revenue increased 32 per cent to MYR3.85bn (US$952m). However, adjusted EBITDA fell 18 per cent to MYR844m (US$209m), mainly due to costs related to the RWNYC launch and a foreign exchange loss.
The result came as the company expanded its casino operations in the United States. Revenue from its US and Bahamas segment rose 166 per cent year-on-year to MYR1.53bn (US$378m), following the launch of full commercial casino operations at Resorts World New York City (RWNYC) in April.
Genting Malaysia said the US market is expected to remain resilient, supported by consumer spending and a steady labour market. In Malaysia, revenue at Resorts World Genting was broadly stable at MYR1.77bn (US$438m), down 1 per cent year-on-year. The company said softer visitation and consumer spending, along with higher payroll costs, affected performance.
Genting Malaysia said it remains cautious about its Malaysian outlook as higher airfares and travel costs continue to put pressure on regional and domestic tourism.

title: Genting Malaysia Stages Recovery But Overseas Expansion Costs Weigh
body:
Genting Malaysia Bhd’s (GENM) earnings recovered sharply quarter-on-quarter in the second quarter ended June 30, 2026 (2QFY26), although profitability remained weighed down by pre-operating costs and higher interest expenses related to its Resorts World New York City (RWNYC) expansion, according to Kenanga Research.

Kenanga said GENM’s core net profit (CNP), excluding RM76 million in non-operating expenses and RM18 million in unrealised foreign exchange losses, stood at RM142 million in 2QFY26, down 40% year-on-year but significantly higher than the RM10 million recorded in 1QFY26.

The research house attributed the quarter-on-quarter recovery largely to the absence of some of the heavy pre-operating expenses incurred in the previous quarter, including recruitment and training costs for RWNYC.

However, higher interest expenses arising from the US$600 million upfront gaming licence payment for RWNYC continued to weigh on profit before tax.

Meanwhile, Resorts World Genting (RWG) and Genting’s UK operations recorded better revenue and EBITDA on a quarter-on-quarter basis, although their year-on-year performance remained broadly flat.

For the first half of FY2026, GENM’s CNP declined 47% year-on-year to RM152 million, with earnings affected by relatively flat EBITDA growth at RWG and weaker performance in the UK.

RWG’s EBITDA was broadly unchanged, rising just 0.2%, while UK EBITDA declined 5%.

RWNYC doubled its US revenue during the first half, but EBITDA increased by only 25% year-on-year as pre-operating expenses continued to weigh on its contribution.

As a result, the improvement at RWNYC was insufficient to offset higher depreciation and interest costs associated with the new property.

GENM’s net debt also increased to RM15.2 billion in 2QFY26, from RM13.7 billion in the previous quarter, resulting in net gearing of 135%.

No dividend was declared for 1HFY26. Kenanga said GENM’s annual dividend per share forecast for FY2026 and FY2027 has been reduced to 5 sen from 7 sen previously.

Despite the near-term earnings pressure, Kenanga remains positive on GENM’s overseas growth prospects, particularly as RWNYC ramps up its casino operations.

RWNYC has commenced casino operations with 242 live gaming tables and 2,465 electronic gaming machines, with plans to increase capacity to 400 live tables and 4,000 machines by the end of FY2026.

Ultimately, the casino is expected to have 800 live tables and 6,000 electronic gaming machines by FY2029.

Kenanga said RWNYC is targeting new gamers, users of John F. Kennedy International Airport and New York players who currently travel to neighbouring states to access casinos offering live gaming.

The research house expects the property’s earnings contribution to improve as operations mature and initial expansion costs stabilise.

GENM’s UK gaming operations are expected to provide another source of earnings growth.

Kenanga noted that the cap on gaming machines at older and smaller UK casinos was increased fourfold to 80 units from July last year.

The acquisition of Aspers Stratford Casinos from administrators and its subsequent relaunch as Genting Stratford Casino has also supported revenue growth.

Although tourism disruption arising from the Middle East conflict could affect the UK market, Kenanga expects the underlying growth momentum to continue.

Expansion-related and restructuring costs, however, have yet to stabilise. Once these costs normalise, the research house expects earnings from the UK business to improve.

Further growth is expected from a new three-storey casino and restaurant at Piccadilly Circus in London, which is scheduled to open in FY2027.

For its flagship RWG operations in Malaysia, Kenanga expects FY2026 earnings to remain subdued, mainly due to weaker overseas tourist arrivals amid the Middle East conflict.

However, relatively resilient domestic visitation should provide some support, particularly in the fourth quarter, when longer school holidays in Malaysia and Singapore are expected to boost visitor traffic.

The extension of the Visit Malaysia Year initiative into 2027 could provide an additional tailwind to tourism-related demand.

Given the slower-than-expected ramp-up at RWNYC and continued high opening costs, Kenanga lowered its FY2026 core earnings per share (CEPS) forecast by 15% to 9.5 sen from 11.2 sen previously.

Its FY2027 CEPS forecast was also cut by 12% to 12.8 sen from 14.5 sen.

Kenanga consequently reduced its target price for GENM by 10% to RM2.70 from RM3.00, based on a price-to-book value multiple of 1.2 times, which is at the upper end of GENM’s historical 10-year range of 1.0 to 1.2 times.

Despite the earnings revisions, Kenanga maintained its Outperform call on GENM, citing what it considers an attractive risk-reward profile.

The research house highlighted GENM’s stronger position at RWNYC, where it expects the group to benefit from being the only full-service casino in New York City for the next three to five years, its increasingly diversified London gaming portfolio and continued upgrades to RWG’s infrastructure and marketing.

Key risks to the investment view include non-renewal of gaming licences, unfavourable prize payout ratios, weaker consumer spending amid elevated inflation and regulatory or social concerns surrounding gaming products.

title: GEN Malaysia U.S. operations seen at 36pct of group EBITDA in 2027: Maybank
body:
Genting Malaysia Bhd’s United States and Caribbean operations are forecast to contribute 36 percent of the group’s annual earnings before interest, taxation, depreciation, and amortisation (EBITDA) in 2027, up 20 percentage points from 2025.

That would be based on a projected 63.1 percent year-on-year increase in the U.S. and Caribbean segment’s EBITDA, to MYR1.45 billion (US$358.5 million) in 2027, from an estimated MYR889.2 million this year, led by performance at the Resorts World New York City (RWNYC) casino complex.

So said Maybank Investment Bank Bhd in a Friday note, following Thursday’s issuance of Genting Malaysia’s second-quarter earnings. The casino firm returned to profit in the period, supported by soaring revenue in the U.S.

“We forecast Genting Malaysia’s U.S. operations – Resorts World New York City, Resorts World Catskills, Resorts World Hudson Valley,” and “Resorts World Bimini” in the Bahamas, “to contribute 36 percent to group EBITDA in full-year 2027 or up 20 percentage points from full-year 2025,” wrote analyst Samuel Yin Shao Yang.

That would translate to MYR1.45 billion, though Genting Malaysia’s flagship Malaysian casino monopoly, Resorts World Genting, was expected to remain the biggest EBITDA contributor for 2027, with MYR2.25 billion.

Maybank said that, in particular, it was “bullish” on RWNYC, in downstate New York.

RWNYC had been an electronic-games venue, but relaunched at the end of April as a full-service casino after winning a full casino licence from the state authorities. The venue will undergo a US$5.5-billion expansion up to 2030, as a condition of its new licence.

“From 242 new tables deployed” at RWNYC “on 28 April 2026, U.S. EBITDA jumped 169 percent quarter-on-quarter to MYR216.6 million,” Mr Yin observed.

The analyst added: “Third-quarter 2026 to date, RWNYC gross gaming revenue (GGR) has also been trending higher as operations ramp up. It plans to raise its table count – including deploying VIP tables – to 400 by early next year.”

The 400 figure had been mentioned by Maybank in a December 2025 note about RWNYC .

“An additional 150 tables is expected to be added by January 2027 in existing space, bringing the total number of table games to 400. The final casino should allow for 6,000 slots and 800 tables by January 2029,” said the investment bank at the time.

While Maybank is bullish on RWNYC, it noted that Genting Malaysia was “cautious” on Resorts World Genting, which currently supplies most of company earnings.

“Second-quarter 2026 Resorts World Genting mass market GGR fell 3 percent year-on-year,” Mr Yin stated.

That was “reflecting cautious consumer spending due to inflation caused by geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and gaming spend diversion to the FIFA World Cup (11 June to 19 July 2026),” added the analyst.

title: [UPDATED] Genting shares fall 6pct after Q2 earnings miss expectations
author: DIYANA ISAMUDIN
body:
KUALA LUMPUR: Genting Bhd's share price fell over six per cent after its second-quarter (Q2) earnings fell short of analysts' expectations.
The stock closed at RM2.10, down 14 sen or 6.25 per cent with more than 17.69 million shares changing hands. This valued the company at about RM8.14 billion.
Year-to-date, Genting's shares have fallen 88 sen, or 29.5 per cent, from RM2.98.
Meanwhile, its 74 per cent-owned unit Genting Malaysia Bhd saw its shares slip one sen or 0.58 per cent to close at RM1.72 per share after reporting a near 90 per cent decline in Q2 net profit to RM47.4 million in Q2 from RM416.6 million in the same period last year.
At current price, Genting Malaysia's market capitalisation stood at RM10 billion.
Genting posted a net loss of RM27 million from RM243.5 million last year, despite revenue rising to RM7.75 billion from RM6.78 billion.
The company attributed the weaker bottom line mainly to foreign exchange translation losses, as well as higher finance and operating costs.
Public Investment Bank Bhd analyst Eltricia Foong said the performances of both Genting and Genting Malaysia came in well below expectations.
This prompted the firm to cut its earnings forecasts for Genting and Genting Malaysia for financial years 2026 to 2028 (FY26-28) by an average of 18 per cent and 11 per cent respectively.
"The operating environment for the entertainment and hospitality industry remains challenging amid rising geopolitical tensions that restrict travel demand and increase operating costs," she said in a note.
PublicInvest maintained a "Neutral" call on both stocks with a target price of RM2.35 for Genting and RM1.73 for Genting Malaysia.
Foong said while earnings are expected to recover gradually, visibility remains weak as geopolitical tensions and slower economic activity could weigh on the global hospitality and entertainment industry.
She expects operating costs to rise in the second half of FY26 due to higher energy costs.
"We do not expect the US operations to deliver higher earnings in the immediate term, in view of the weakening job market and consumer confidence," she said.
Foong also raised concerns over Genting's gearing level given the heavy capital commitments of its subsidiaries, Genting Malaysia and Genting Singapore, for their development projects at Resorts World New York City and Resorts World Sentosa.
On Genting Malaysia, she said the full-scale expansion of its New York casino could eventually act as a catalyst, but was unlikely to be earnings-accretive over the next one to two years given its hefty US$5.5 billion project cost.
Resorts World New York City launched its first table games on April 28, ahead of its competitors, which could help boost gross gaming revenue.
However, Foong expects operating costs to rise amid inflationary pressures in the US.
She also cautioned that continued de-dollarisation could erode the value of the company's US dollar investments over time if future gross gaming revenue fails to match historical growth rates.
She added that changing consumer preferences, particularly younger consumers' increasing preference for online gaming platforms over traditional physical casinos, could affect Genting Malaysia's long-term growth prospects.

title: Stock Today: Genting Malaysia Falls 1.16% As Resorts World Genting Recovery In Focus
body:
Genting Malaysia Bhd (GENM) fell 2 sen or 1.16% to RM1.71 as at 11.30am on Friday, with 13.23 million shares traded, as investors weighed the stock’s near-term performance against expectations of a stronger second half of 2026.

The stock opened at RM1.72 and moved between RM1.70 and RM1.72, with 1.19 million shares queued on the buy side at RM1.71 against 2.55 million shares offered at RM1.72. Its last traded price compared with the previous close of RM1.73.

CIMB Securities has retained its BUY call on GENM with a RM2.50 target price, making it the research house’s top pick in Malaysia’s gaming sector despite maintaining a Neutral view on the sector.

CIMB expects Resorts World Genting’s visitor numbers to return to year-on-year growth in 2H26 as domestic tourism strengthens, while GENM’s US casino operations are expected to provide additional earnings support.

Resorts World New York City began full-scale casino operations on 28 April, with weekly gross gaming revenue rising around 49% in its first eight weeks compared with the second quarter of 2025.

CIMB expects GENM’s earnings recovery to accelerate in 2027, forecasting core earnings per share to surge 125% as the New York operation ramps up. The stock’s forecast 2027 enterprise value-to-EBITDA multiple of 7.3 times also represents a 22% discount to its pre-pandemic 10-year historical average.

title: Genting shares slip in early trade after 2Q earnings miss
body:
KUALA LUMPUR (Aug 21): Genting Bhd's (KL:GENTING) shares fell nearly 5% on Friday morning after its second financial quarter ended June 30, 2026 (2QFY2026) came in below analysts’ expectations.
The counter declined to RM2.14 per share, valuing the group at RM8.3 billion, with some 7.16 million shares changing hands.
Meanwhile, the group's 74%-owned subsidiary Genting Malaysia (KL:GENM) saw its shares slipping 1.2% to RM1.71 per share after announcing a near 90% drop in net profit to RM47.4 million in 2QFY2026 from RM416.6 million in the same period last year.
Genting recorded a net loss of RM27 million from a profit of RM243.5 million in the same period in 2025, despite higher revenue of RM7.75 billion from RM6.78 billion the year prior. This was attributed to forex translation losses, as well as higher finance and operating costs.
Public Investment Bank noted that both performances fell well below its expectations, prompting it to cut its FY2026-FY2028 earnings forecasts for Genting and Genting Malaysia by an average of 18% and 11% respectively.
“The operating environment for the entertainment and hospitality industry remains challenging amid rising geopolitical tensions that restrict travel demand and increase operating costs,” said Public Investment in a note, which has a 'neutral' call on both stocks.
Hong Leong Investment Bank (HLIB) flagged that both the companies could face further decline from ongoing Iran war-related disruptions, such as higher airfares and potential flight cancellations, which may dampen discretionary travel demand to regional leisure assets.
Following the results shortfall, HLIB trimmed its FY2026-FY2028 forecasts for Genting by 31.2%/28.1%/25% respectively, mainly to reflect downward revisions for Genting Malaysia.
For Genting Malaysia, it cut its FY2026-FY2028 forecasts by 40.4%/29.8%/18.2% respectively to primarily account for lower Ebitda margins assumptions for both the UK and Egypt and the US and Bahamas operations.
HLIB kept its 'hold' call on Genting Malaysia with a lower target price of RM1.74 while downgrading Genting to 'hold' with a target price of RM2.02.

title: Genting Berhad posts 2Q26 net loss despite 67% rise in US revenue
author: Viviana Chan
body:
Malaysian conglomerate Genting Berhad, the parent company of Genting Malaysia Berhad and Genting Singapore Limited, swung to a second-quarter net loss attributable to shareholders despite stronger revenue and growth from its US casino operations.
The group recorded a net loss of MYR27.1 million ($6.7 million), compared with a MYR243.5 million profit a year earlier, according to results released on Thursday.
Revenue rose 14 percent year-on-year to MYR7.75 billion ($1.92 billion), while adjusted EBITDA increased 2 percent to MYR2.12 billion ($524.5 million). Profit before tax fell 46 percent to MYR569.6 million ($141 million), partly due to higher finance costs and lower interest income.
Maybank Investment Bank said the results ‘missed our expectations,’ with second-quarter core profit of MYR145.1 million bringing the first-half total to MYR260.6 million, or 35 percent of its full-year estimate.
The brokerage said the earnings shortfall was exacerbated by higher-than-expected net interest expenses. It subsequently reduced its Genting core profit forecasts for 2026 through 2028 by between 20 percent and 26 percent.
Maybank described the group’s US operations as ‘a tale of two stories,’ with the ramp-up of Resorts World New York City contrasting with sequential weakness at Resorts World Las Vegas.
Revenue from Genting’s US and Bahamas leisure and hospitality segment increased 67 percent to MYR2.26 billion ($559.4 million), while EBITDA rose 56 percent to MYR313.3 million ($77.5 million).
Maybank said the 242 gaming tables introduced at Resorts World New York City on April 28th helped US EBITDA rise 56 percent year-on-year and 12 percent quarter-on-quarter.
The brokerage said the property’s gross gaming revenue had continued to trend higher during the third quarter. Resorts World New York City plans to increase its table count to 400 by early 2027, including the deployment of VIP tables.
By contrast, Resorts World Las Vegas EBITDA declined 52 percent quarter-on-quarter to $24 million. Genting attributed the sequential decline to seasonal softness, according to Maybank.
The brokerage expects the Las Vegas property to improve in the second half of 2026, supported by a stronger convention calendar and the Formula 1 Las Vegas Grand Prix in November.
Maybank expects Genting’s second-half core profit to be slightly higher than in the first half, supported by the New York ramp-up and a seasonal recovery in Las Vegas. The improvement could be moderated by potentially lower VIP win rates at Resorts World Genting.
Genting did not declare an interim dividend, citing ongoing investments, business requirements and efforts to reduce existing debt.

title: Genting Malaysia returns to profit in 2Q, as U.S. revenue soars and domestic performance is flat
body:
Global casino operator Genting Malaysia Bhd reported a profit of MYR27.0 million (US$6.7 million) for the second quarter of 2026. That was an improvement on the MYR25.2-million loss it recorded for the first three months of 2026, but far from the MYR398.1 million profit of the second quarter of 2025.

The quarterly profit was helped by a 32.6 percent year-on-year increase in group-wide revenues from leisure and hospitality operations, to nearly MYR3.81 billion, the company said in a Thursday filing to Bursa Malaysia.

The firm decided not to declare an interim dividend for the period.

“The group will continue to exercise prudent capital management, balancing business requirements and ongoing investments with efforts to pare down existing debt, with a focus on delivering sustainable long-term value to shareholders,” it said.

Genting Malaysia noted that its quarterly performance benefited from the commencement of the initial phase of full commercial casino operations at Resorts World New York City on April 28, with the introduction of live table gaming and slot machines.

The property continued its “phased commercial casino rollout” with 1,400 additional slot machines coming online in July, Genting Malaysia said in a press release accompanying its second-quarter results.

Genting Malaysia said, fuelled by Resorts World New York City’s performance, revenue for its United States and the Bahamas segment more than doubled year-on-year, to MYR1.53 billion, while adjusted earnings before interest, taxation, depreciation, and amortisation (EBITDA) for the segment increased by circa 82.9 percent to MYR216.6 million.

The Resorts World New York City property (pictured) in Queens, New York City, was previously an electronic gaming venue. The complex, run by a unit of Genting Malaysia, is being upgraded and expanded as a full-scale casino resort after the group was awarded a full casino licence by the New York State Gaming Commission.

Genting Malaysia’s latest quarterly results also included a full-quarter contribution from Genting Casino Stratford in the U.K. capital, London, acquired in April 2025, as well as Empire Resorts Inc, included in the group’s operations in May 2025.

The firm reported group-wide adjusted EBITDA of MYR844.0 million in the second quarter this year, 18.0-percent lower than in the prior-year period.

The decline was mainly due to the recognition of a net unrealised forex loss of MYR18.1 million in the second quarter of 2026, compared with forex gains of MYR184.6 million a year earlier, “arising from the translation of the group’s U.S. dollar-denominated borrowings”, Genting Malaysia stated.

Excluding this impact, adjusted EBITDA would have hit MYR862.1 million.

Malaysia performance flat

Genting Malaysia has a Malaysian casino monopoly at Resorts World Genting, near that country’s capital Kuala Lumpur, and also runs casinos in the United Kingdom and Egypt, and the United States and the Bahamas.

Genting Malaysia reported a 71.4 percent year-on-year decline in profit before taxation to MYR143.8 million, which was “partly attributable to ramp-up costs, higher depreciation and higher financing costs for the development of Resorts World New York City’s commercial casino project.”

Second-quarter revenue in the Malaysia leisure and hospitality segment, including the casino operation, was MYR1.77 billion, compared to MYR1.78 billion a year earlier. Adjusted EBITDA improved marginally to MYR615.0 million, from MYR606.3 million in the second quarter of 2025.

“The performance was mainly impacted by softer visitation and consumer spending, as well as higher payroll costs,” Genting Malaysia said. Adjusted EBITDA margin was 35 percent in the second quarter of 2026, one percentage point higher than a year earlier.

For the first six months of 2026, Genting Malaysia reported total revenue of MYR6.72 billion, an increase of 21.9 percent from the same period last year. Adjusted EBITDA declined by 15.7 percent, to MYR1.49 billion, while net profit stood at MYR1.8 million, compared with a net profit of MYR450.1 million in the opening half of 2025.

In Thursday’s filing, Genting Malaysia said the global economic environment remained “uncertain” amid “renewed geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and macroeconomic risks”.

The firm said it remained “cautious” about the business outlook in Malaysia, as “regional and domestic tourism are expected to remain under pressure as higher airfares and travel-related fuel costs continue to weigh on consumer travel decisions.”

Genting Malaysia said it was focused on “operational discipline and yield management” domestically, while investing “selectively” in infrastructure, attractions and new experiences at Resorts World Genting to “broaden its offerings and strengthen its competitiveness”.

The company, however, added it expected the United States market “to remain resilient, underpinned by robust consumer spending and a steady labour market.”

title: U.S. segment, expansion of Resorts World NYC, lift Genting Malaysia revenue in Q2
author: Inside Asian Gaming
body:
Costs related to the launch of full casino operations at Resorts World New York City (RWNYC) in April saw Genting Malaysia report a narrowed profit of MYR27.0 million (US$6.7 million) in the three months to 30 June 2026, down from MYR398.1 million (US$98.4 million) a year earlier.
However, it also saw revenue soar. While Genting Malaysia did not break down its US revenue by property, the company’s US and Bahamas segment reported a 166% year-on-year increase in revenue to MYR1.53 billion (US$378 million) – helping group-wide revenue rise 32% to MYR3.85 billion (US$952 million). This was despite Resorts World Genting (RWG) in Malaysia seeing a slight 1% decline in revenue to MYR1.77 billion (US$438 million) and the UK and Egypt also seeing a 1% fall to MYR506.2 million (US$125 million).

title: Genting Malaysia borrowings rise 23% as New York casino costs squeeze profit
author: Viviana Chan
body:
Genting Malaysia’s total borrowings rose 23 percent in the first half of 2026, as financing and ramp-up costs associated with its Resorts World New York City casino expansion weighed on profitability, according to the company’s latest financial results released on Thursday, August 20th.
Borrowings increased to MYR15.70 billion ($3.85 billion) at the end of June, from MYR12.72 billion ($3.12 billion) at the end of 2025.
The results showed that second-quarter net profit attributable to shareholders fell 89 percent year-on-year to MYR47.4 million ($11.6 million), despite a 32 percent increase in revenue to MYR3.85 billion ($944 million).
Adjusted EBITDA declined 18 percent to MYR844 million ($207 million), largely due to an unrealized foreign-exchange loss compared with a sizeable gain in the previous-year period. Excluding the currency impact, adjusted EBITDA increased 2 percent to MYR862.1 million ($211 million).
During the first half, Genting New York drew $755 million from a secured credit facility to fund the commercial casino license fee and capital expenditure at Resorts World New York City.
Genting Americas also entered into a new $2 billion secured credit facility in June to refinance existing New York debt, redeem $300 million in notes issued by Empire Resorts and support the development and operation of the Queens casino.
New York operations expand
Revenue from Genting Malaysia’s United States and Bahamas segment more than doubled to MYR1.53 billion ($376 million) in the second quarter, while adjusted EBITDA increased 83 percent to MYR216.6 million ($53.1 million).
The improvement was primarily attributed to the launch of full commercial casino operations at Resorts World New York City on April 28th. The property opened with 242 gaming tables and 2,500 slot machines before adding another 1,400 slots in July.
However, the expansion also contributed to higher pre-operating expenses, depreciation and financing costs. Group finance costs rose 43 percent to MYR281 million ($68.9 million) during the quarter.
Genting Malaysia disclosed MYR15.36 billion ($3.76 billion) in authorized capital commitments not provided for in its financial statements. This included MYR12.56 billion ($3.08 billion) in development expenditure related to Resorts World New York City.
The company said it would continue exercising ‘prudent capital management’, balancing ongoing investments with efforts to reduce existing debt.
In Malaysia, second-quarter leisure and hospitality revenue slipped 1 percent to MYR1.77 billion ($433 million), affected by softer visitation and consumer spending. The group remains cautious about the market’s near-term outlook, citing higher airfares and travel-related fuel costs.

title: Genting revenue grows to RM7.75bil in 2Q26
author: Eugene  Mahalingam
body:
PETALING JAYA: Genting Bhd expects the global economic environment to remain uncertain, as renewed geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and macroeconomic risks continue weighing on the growth outlook.
Against this backdrop, the group said in a filing with Bursa Malaysia that it remains cautious of the near-term prospects in Malaysia and continues to monitor the operating environment closely in order to navigate these near-term headwinds.
“Nonetheless, certain major economies, such as the United States, are expected to remain resilient, underpinned by robust consumer spending and a steady labour market,” it said.
For its second quarter ended June 30, 2026 (2Q26), Genting reported a net loss of RM27.1mil, compared with a net profit of RM243.5mil in the previous corresponding period, due to higher finance costs, lower interest income, lower share of profits in joint ventures and associates and higher depreciation, partly mitigated by lower net impairment losses.
Revenue in 2Q26 rose to RM7.75bil from RM6.78bil previously, driven by its leisure and hospitality and plantation division.
The group’s adjusted earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (Ebitda) for 2Q26 of RM2.1bil was higher by 2% compared with 2Q25.
“The strengthening of the ringgit against the Singapore dollar, British pound, and US dollar partly reduced the translated contributions of revenue and Ebitda in ringgit from foreign operations in 2Q26.”
Genting added that Resorts World Sentosa (RWS) continued to make good progress in 2Q26 as RWS advanced its transformation into a refreshed lifestyle destination. “Supported by new offerings and operational resilience, business performance improved notwithstanding geopolitical uncertainties.
“RWS reported improvements in revenue and Ebitda. However, after translation into ringgit, the revenue was lower and Ebitda was on par compared with 2Q25, mainly due to the strengthening of ringgit against the Singapore dollar.”
For the six-month period ended June 30, 2026, net profit plunged to RM74mil from RM248.1mil in the previous corresponding period, while revenue rose to RM14.41bil from RM13.29bil a year earlier.
Genting said RWS’ revenue was broadly stable year-on-year for the first half of financial year 2026 (1H26), as higher non-gaming revenue was partly offset by lower gaming revenue at the Singapore Integrated Resort.
“Growth in non-gaming revenue was supported by refreshed attractions, hospitality and experiential offerings even as tourism conditions weakened.
“Ebitda decreased compared with 1H25.
“Earnings were supported by steady operational progress and continued asset optimisation efforts. The strengthening of the ringgit against the Singapore dollar reduced the translated contributions of revenue and Ebitda in ringgit in 1H26.”
Meanwhile, the group’s subsidiary, Genting Malaysia Bhd, saw its net profit in 2Q26 plunge to RM47.4mil from RM416.6mil in the previous corresponding period.
“The group’s underlying operating performance continued to reflect a softer operating environment, in line with broader trends observed across similar markets regionally.
“The period was affected by moderating travel demand and more measured consumer spending amid prolonged geopolitical tensions in the Middle East.
“The group’s performance was also impacted by inflationary cost pressures during the quarter,” it said.
Revenue in 2Q26 rose to RM3.85bil from RM2.92bil previously.
“Notwithstanding the increase in revenue, adjusted Ebitda declined by 18% to RM844mil, mainly due to the recognition of a net unrealised foreign exchange (forex) translation loss of RM18.1mil in 2Q26, compared with forex gains of RM184.6mil in 2Q25, arising from the translation of the group’s US dollar-denominated borrowings.
“Excluding this impact, adjusted Ebitda increased by 2% to RM862.1mil,” it said.
For the six-month period ended June 30, 2026, net profit plunged to RM43.6mil from RM489.3mil in the previous corresponding period, while revenue rose to RM6.72bil from RM5.51bil previously.
Genting Malaysia said the lower profit was partially attributable to costs associated with the commencement and ramp-up of; Resorts World New York City’s full commercial casino operations, higher depreciation and higher financing costs for the development of the integrated resort.

title: Genting Bhd’s Resorts World Las Vegas shows incremental improvement in 2Q26 on convention business and improved premium play
body:
Genting Berhad’s US flagship Resorts World Las Vegas (RWLV) made some small strides in the three months to 30 June 2026, with revenue rising by 1% year-on-year to US$181 million and EBITDA climbing 33% to US$24 million.
The result was, however, down from the March quarter with revenue falling 13% and EBITDA considerably lower than the US$50 million reported in Q1.
In its 2Q26 earnings report, parent company Genting Bhd noted that RWLV’s revenue and EBITDA benefitted from increased conventions attendance, with hotel occupancy of 88.0% improved from 80.2% a year earlier and Average Daily Rate of US$274 respectively improved from US$265. It also pointed to an increased volume of high-end casino play.
According to Genting Bhd, “RWLV expects convention booking trends to remain robust due to its close proximity to the Las Vegas Convention Center and established convention business.
“RWLV expects gaming results to continue to improve as it continues to grow high-end hosted casino play and resort marketing initiatives to attract high-value guests. On the non-gaming side, RWLV is working to develop distinctive brand experiences and right-size value proposition to maximise margin and align with guest expectations. The property will continue to leverage its enhanced hotel system to extend its reach to customers and implement tailored casino offerings to drive repeat visitation.
“RWLV remains focused on improving margins through refining productivity and optimising the fixed cost structure, which includes evaluating business hours of operation and right-size workforce across all areas to meet guest demands. RWLV is also evaluating new opportunities to invest in new dining concepts and performances at the Resorts World Theatre.”
For the June 2026 quarter, Genting Bhd – which counts Genting Malaysia and Genting Singapore among its core subsidiaries – reported a 14% year-on-year increase in revenue to MYR7.75 billion (US$1.92 billion), aided by the opening of full casino operations at Resorts World New York City (RWNYC) in April. RWNYC operates under Genting Malaysia.
Group-wide Adjusted EBITDA grew by 2% year-on-year to MYR2.12 billion (US$524 million) while profit fell by 71% to MYR197.6 million (US$48,8 million) due to depreciation and interest costs.

title: Genting Malaysia reports 166% rise in US segment revenue to US$378 million in 2Q26 after Resorts World New York City opening, li
body:
Costs related to the launch of full casino operations at Resorts World New York City (RWNYC) in April saw Genting Malaysia report a narrowed profit of MYR27.0 million (US$6.7 million) in the three months to 30 June 2026, down from MYR398.1 million (US$98.4 million) a year earlier.
However, it also saw revenue soar. While Genting Malaysia did not break down its US revenue by property, the company’s US and Bahamas segment reported a 166% year-on-year increase in revenue to MYR1.53 billion (US$378 million) – helping group-wide revenue rise 32% to MYR3.85 billion (US$952 million). This was despite Resorts World Genting (RWG) in Malaysia seeing a slight 1% decline in revenue to MYR1.77 billion (US$438 million) and the UK and Egypt also seeing a 1% fall to MYR506.2 million (US$125 million).
Group-wide Adjusted EBITDA was down 18% year-on-year to MYR844 million (US$209 million) although this reflected RWNYC opening costs as well as the recognition of a Forex loss compared with a substantial gain in 2Q25.
In a note, Nomura analysts observed that US-segment revenue was up 121% compared with the March 2026 quarter, with Adjusted EBITDA up 169%.
RWNYC launched downstate New York’s first casino table games on 28 April, offering 242 table games and 2,500 slot machines, before adding another 1,400 slot machines last month. It also broke ground on the next phase of the US$5.5 billion RWNYC expansion in late July.
At RWG, revenue of MYR1.77 billion (US$438 million), while down year-on-year, was 6% higher quarter-on-quarter with Adjusted EBITDA up 20% sequentially to MYR615 million (US$214 million) thanks in part to a higher VIP win rate.
In a note, Nomura’s Tushar Mohata and Alpa Aggarwal said they consider the Malaysia results to be a “positive surprise, given the disruptions caused by the war in the Middle East to flights and tourist arrivals.”
In its earnings release, Genting Malaysia said, “The global economic environment remains uncertain, as renewed geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and macroeconomic risks continue weighing on the growth outlook. Against this backdrop, the Group remains cautious of the near-term prospects in Malaysia and continues to monitor the operating environment closely in order to navigate these near-term headwinds.”
It added, “For Malaysia, regional and domestic tourism are expected to remain under pressure as higher airfares and travel-related fuel costs continue to weigh on consumer travel decisions. The Group is focused on operational discipline and yield management to optimise performance and manage costs, whilst continuing to enhance RWG’s integrated resort offerings to drive visitation and customer engagement. The Group continues to invest selectively in infrastructure, attractions and new experiences to broaden its offerings and strengthen its competitiveness.”

title: Malaysia’s Genting posts Q2 net loss despite 14% rise in revenue
author: Tan Ai Leng
body:
Malaysia’s Genting posts Q2 net loss despite 14% rise in revenue
External headwinds, rising costs and a stronger ringgit drag conglomerate into the red in Q2
[KUALA LUMPUR] Malaysia’s Genting Berhad swung into the red in the second quarter despite double-digit revenue growth, as the conglomerate grappled with rising costs and a stronger ringgit, even as its casino businesses showed signs of improvement in their key markets.
The group posted a net loss of RM27.1 million (US$6.7 million) for the three months ended June, reversing a net profit of RM243.5 million in the year before.
Its revenue rose 14.2 per cent to RM7.7 billion from RM6.8 billion.
For the first six months, revenue grew 9 per cent year on year to RM14.4 billion, and net profit fell 70 per cent to RM74 million.
Genting attributed the higher quarterly revenue to its plantation business, driven by higher production and improved downstream manufacturing sales, as well as its leisure and hospitality operations in Singapore and Malaysia.
The stronger ringgit, however, weighed on its overseas businesses. Genting said that the currency’s appreciation against the Singapore dollar, British pound and US dollar reduced the translated revenue and adjusted earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (Ebitda) contributions from foreign operations during the quarter.
Genting Malaysia (GENM), the subsidiary that manages the group’s casino businesses in Malaysia, the UK and the US, similarly recorded stronger revenue but sharply weaker earnings.
Its Q2 revenue jumped 31.9 per cent to RM3.8 billion, but its net profit plunged 88.6 per cent to RM47.4 million.
For the first six months, GENM’s revenue rose 22 per cent to RM6.7 billion, while its net profit dropped 91 per cent to RM43.6 million.
Genting and GENM did not declare an interim dividend, saying that it would balance its business requirements and ongoing investments with efforts to pare down existing debt.
Tradeview Capital portfolio manager Neoh Jia Man was pessimistic about the near-term earnings outlook for both Genting and GENM, pointing to geopolitical tensions, higher travel costs and the ongoing expansion of Resorts World New York City (RWNYC).
He told The Business Times: “The Middle East conflict could weigh on casino visitor numbers through flight disruptions and travel-cost inflation, while startup costs at RWNYC are likely to remain elevated for another one to two quarters.”
Nevertheless, New York is emerging as a bright spot for Genting’s casino business.
Genting’s US and Bahamas leisure and hospitality operations, excluding Resorts World Las Vegas, recorded higher revenue and Ebitda, primarily following the start of full commercial casino operations at RWNYC on Apr 28.
The property launched with 242 table games and 2,500 slot machines, with another 1,400 slots subsequently added. GENM broke ground in July on the next phase of development to transform RWNYC into a full-scale integrated resort for gaming, entertainment and hospitality.
Early operating data suggests the table-game roll-out is gaining traction.
In a recent report, Maybank Investment Bank Research said that weekly gross gaming revenue (GGR) from table games has climbed to US$11.1 million, from US$4.9 million in the opening week.
Average daily GGR per table reached US$6,539, above Maybank’s US$5,500 forecast. Despite 12 per cent cannibalisation of slot GGR, Maybank noted that the shift towards table games, taxed at 30 per cent versus 56 per cent for slots, is positive.
It estimates the lower slot tax could add US$120 million to annual Ebitda, with US operations contributing 36 per cent of GENM’s Ebitda by 2027.
Analysts warned the expansion of RWNYC carries sizeable near-term costs. CGS International estimates GENM’s 2026 capital expenditure at about US$1 billion for New York licence fee and pre-operating costs. Interest on the facility used to fund the licence is being expensed rather than capitalised, which CGS said would continue weigh on near-term earnings.
Elsewhere, Genting’s casino operations showed signs of improvement.
Resorts World Sentosa (RWS) recorded higher revenue and Ebitda in Singapore-dollar terms, but a stronger ringgit erased the gains, with ringgit revenue falling and Ebitda remaining flat year on year.
Neoh said that Genting’s broad geographical exposure gives it a more balanced portfolio, but also leaves the group exposed to foreign-exchange translation risk.
Its overseas casinos also face greater competitive pressure than Resorts World Genting, which holds Malaysia’s sole casino licence.
Resorts World Las Vegas benefited from stronger convention attendance and improved high-end play. Hotel occupancy rose to 88 per cent from 80.2 per cent the year before, while its average daily rate rose to US$274 from US$265.
Genting expects convention attendance in Las Vegas to reach a record high in 2026 following the completed expansion of the Las Vegas Convention Center, which increased its capacity by 30 per cent.
The group remains cautious about the outlook, warning that geopolitical tensions and macroeconomic risks continue to cloud global growth; in Malaysia, higher airfares and travel-related fuel costs could weigh on regional and domestic tourism.

title: Genting swings into 2Q loss as higher finance costs, absence of one-off gain weigh
body:
KUALA LUMPUR (Aug 20): Genting Bhd (KL:GENTING) slipped into a loss in the second quarter despite increased revenue and operating earnings, as higher finance costs and an absence of significant disposal gains recorded a year earlier weighed on its bottom line.
The diversified gaming and leisure group posted a net loss of RM27.10 million for the three months ended June 30, 2026 (2QFY2026), compared with a net profit of RM243.50 million a year earlier. Revenue, however, rose 14% to RM7.75 billion from RM6.78 billion, thanks to the group's leisure and hospitality, and plantation business.
Genting attributed the huge decline mainly to higher finance costs and depreciation, lower interest income and smaller share of profits from its joint venture and associates. The year-ago quarter also included a RM338.3 million gain from the disposal of assets classified as held for sale.
At one of its resorts, Resorts World Genting, the group managed to report higher Ebitda despite lower revenue, helped by operating cost management. This was despite higher payroll expenses following the renewal of a union agreement that offset the improvement.
Meanwhile, in the US, the initial phase of full commercial casino operations with the introduction of live table gaming and slot machines at Resorts World New York City (RWNYC), which began on April 28, helped lift revenue. Separately, the group's Resorts World Las Vegas also benefitted from increased convention attendance and stronger high-end gaming activity.
Genting's plantation division also reported higher revenue on increased fresh fruit bunch production, while its downstream manufacturing business benefitted from stronger sales volumes and margins.
Separately, Genting's 73.9%-owned subsidiary Genting Malaysia Bhd (KL:GENM) reported an 89% plunge in net profit to RM47.4 million for 2QFY2026 from RM416.6 million a year earlier.
Revenue nevertheless jumped 32% to RM3.85 billion from RM2.92 billion, mainly due to contributions from the commencement of commercial casino operations at RWNYC, as well as from the acquired Genting Casino Stratford and consolidated Genting Empire Resorts LLC.
The decline in net profit was partly driven by less favourable foreign-exchange comparison. Genting Malaysia recorded a RM18.1 million unrealised forex translation loss on its US dollar-denominated borrowings in 2QFY2026, compared with a RM184.6 million translation gain a year earlier.
Genting Malaysia said it remains cautious about near-term prospects in Malaysia amid higher airfares and travel-related fuel costs, which could weigh on domestic and regional tourism.
"The group is focused on operational discipline and yield management to optimise performance and manage costs, whilst continuing to enhance Resorts World Genting’s integrated resort offerings to drive visitation and customer engagement," it said.
In New York, RWNYC launched its full commercial casino operations with 242 table games and 2,500 slot machines in April, with another 1,400 slot machines subsequently added. Genting Malaysia broke ground in July on the next phase of the project, which is intended to transform RWNYC into a full-scale integrated resort encompassing gaming, entertainment and hospitality.
For the first half of FY2026, Genting's revenue rose 8% to RM14.41 billion, but net profit fell 70% to RM74 million from RM248.1 million. Genting Malaysia, meanwhile, saw first-half revenue rise 22% to RM6.72 billion, while net profit plunged 91% to RM43.6 million from RM489.3 million.
Neither Genting nor Genting Malaysia declared an interim dividend for the first half.
Shares of Genting settled four sen or 1.82% higher at RM2.24 on Thursday, valuing the group at RM8.68 billion. Meanwhile, Genting Malaysia settled one sen or 0.57% lower at RM1.73, giving it a market capitalisation of RM10.27 billion.

title: Genting swings to RM27.1m net loss in 2Q as finance costs, forex weigh
author: Dayang Norazhar
body:
GENTING Bhd swung to a net loss of RM27.1 million for the second quarter ended June 30, 2026 (2Q26), from a net profit of RM243.5 million a year earlier, despite a 14% increase in quarterly revenue.
The weaker bottom line was mainly due to higher finance costs, lower interest income, lower share of profits from joint ventures and associates, and higher depreciation, Genting said in its results announcement today.
The group’s 2Q26 profit before tax fell 46% to RM569.6 million from RM1.05 billion previously.
The year-ago quarter had also included a RM338.3 million gain on the disposal of assets classified as held for sale.
Revenue rose to RM7.75 billion from RM6.78 billion, driven mainly by the Leisure & Hospitality and Plantation divisions.
Adjusted earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) rose 2% to RM2.12 billion from RM2.08 billion previously, although the strengthening of the ringgit against the Singapore dollar, pound sterling and US dollar partly reduced the translated contributions from its overseas operations.
For the six months ended June 30, 1HFY2026 net profit fell 70.2% to RM74 million from RM248.1 million, while revenue increased 8.4% to RM14.41 billion from RM13.29 billion.
Profit before tax for the period declined 38.2% to RM1.03 billion from RM1.67 billion, while adjusted EBITDA slipped 3% to RM3.94 billion.
Genting said Resorts World Sentosa (RWS) continued to make progress in the second quarter, with improvements in revenue and EBITDA in Singapore dollar terms, supported by new offerings and operational resilience.
However, after translation into ringgit, revenue was lower while EBITDA was broadly unchanged from a year earlier due to the stronger ringgit.
Resorts World Genting recorded higher EBITDA despite lower revenue, mainly due to operating cost management.
The improvement was partly offset by higher payroll costs following the renewal of its contracted union agreement.
Its UK and Egypt leisure and hospitality businesses recorded marginally lower revenue and EBITDA, mainly due to geopolitical tensions in the Middle East affecting premium gaming segments and higher payroll costs arising from increases in national minimum wages.
In the US and Bahamas, revenue and EBITDA increased excluding Resorts World Las Vegas, primarily due to the commencement of full commercial casino operations at Resorts World New York City (RWNYC) on April 28, 2026.
RWNYC introduced live table gaming and slot machines during the quarter, compared with a video gaming machine-only facility in 2Q25.
The contribution was partly offset by higher operating and payroll costs as the casino ramps up its commercial operations.
Genting said Resorts World Las Vegas benefited from higher convention attendance and improved high-end play.
Hotel occupancy rose to 88% in 2Q26 from 80.2% a year earlier, while average daily rate increased to US$274 from US$265.
Its oil palm plantation business recorded higher revenue and EBITDA, mainly due to higher fresh fruit bunch production, while the downstream manufacturing segment also posted higher revenue and EBITDA on improved sales volumes and margins.
The power division’s revenue and EBITDA in ringgit were lower due to the stronger ringgit against the US dollar, although its US dollar performance improved on higher generation from the Banten plant in Indonesia.
Meanwhile, the oil and gas division’s revenue fell and it reported an adjusted LBITDA following the expiry of the petroleum contract of Genting CDX Singapore Pte Ltd in the Chengdaoxi Block on April 15, 2026.
Looking ahead, Genting said the global economic environment remains uncertain, with renewed geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and macroeconomic risks weighing on the growth outlook.
In Malaysia, Genting Malaysia Bhd remains cautious on the near-term prospects as regional and domestic tourism could remain under pressure from higher airfares and travel-related fuel costs.
The group said it will focus on operational discipline and yield management, while continuing to enhance Resorts World Genting’s integrated resort offerings.
In the US, Genting Malaysia is focused on the phased development of RWNYC.
It said it had launched full commercial casino operations comprising 242 table games and 2,500 slot machines in April, with a further 1,400 slot machines subsequently added.
The group broke ground in July for the next phase of RWNYC’s development, which aims to transform the property into a full-scale integrated resort encompassing gaming, entertainment and hospitality.
Genting Singapore, meanwhile, continues to execute its RWS 2.0 transformation, with further enhancements to Hotel Michael, Crockfords Tower, the casino, selected restaurants and key public spaces expected to be introduced progressively in 2027 and 2028. –TMR

title: Genting outlook faces mixed road ahead as Q2 profit falls sharply
author: Business Times
body:
KUALA LUMPUR: Genting Bhd's second-quarter net profit falls sharply but the group expects its businesses to navigate a mixed operating environment for the rest of 2026.
The group expects growth in the US, Singapore and plantation businesses to be tempered by geopolitical risks, softer tourism demand and rising costs.
Genting's net profit shrank to RM197.6 million in the second quarter ended June 30 2026 from RM680.8 million a year earlier, although revenue rose 14 per cent to RM7.75 billion.
For the first half, its net profit fell to RM414.8 million from RM958.4 million previously, while revenue increased eight per cent to RM14.41 billion.
Genting said Resorts World New York City (RWNYC) would be a key growth driver following the start of full commercial casino operations in April.
The casino opened with 242 table games and 2,500 slot machines, with another 1,400 slot machines subsequently added.
The group said Genting Malaysia Bhd also broke ground in July for the next phase to transform RWNYC into a full-scale integrated resort.
The US and Bahamas businesses recorded higher revenue and EBITDA in the second quarter, excluding Resorts World Las Vegas, supported by RWNYC and the consolidation of Genting Empire Resorts.
Resorts World Sentosa (RWS) continued to see progress from its transformation programme, although gaming revenue was softer in the first half.
Genting Singapore is continuing work under its RWS 2.0 strategy, with upgrades to hotels, the casino, restaurants and public areas scheduled progressively through 2027 and 2028.
The company expects the transformation to be completed by 2030, broadly aligning with Singapore's Greater Sentosa Master Plan.
Resorts World Las Vegas recorded stronger performance, supported by increased convention attendance and higher-end gaming.
Hotel occupancy rose to 88 per cent in the second quarter from 80.2 per cent a year earlier, while average daily rate increased to US$274 from US$265.
Genting expects convention demand to remain firm, helped by the expanded Las Vegas Convention Center, while focusing on improving margins and controlling fixed costs.
In Malaysia, Resorts World Genting posted higher Ebitda despite lower revenue, helped by cost management.
However, Genting Malaysia expects tourism demand to remain under pressure from higher airfares and travel-related fuel costs.
It plans to focus on yield management, cost discipline and new attractions to support visitation.
The plantation division benefited from higher fresh fruit bunch production, although lower crude palm oil prices moderated the gains.
Genting Plantations expects palm oil prices to remain supported by biofuel mandates and firmer energy prices, but warned that higher production and weaker demand from major importers could limit further upside.
Genting said it would not declare an interim dividend for the current quarter, citing the need to balance investment requirements, business needs and debt reduction.
The group said it would continue exercising prudent capital management while focusing on sustainable long-term value.

title: Genting Malaysia dissolves Macau-incorporated subsidiary that bid for Macau gaming concession in 2022
body:
Genting Malaysia has begun the process to dissolve a subsidiary it previously incorporated in Macau as part of its unsuccessful efforts to win a gaming concession in the Special Administrative Region back in 2022.
In a filing, the Malaysian casino operator said that shareholders in its dormant wholly-owned subsidiary GMM Limited had resolved to dissolve the entity and that a voluntary liquidation had begun. Relevant documents were submitted to the Commerce and Movable Property Registry of Macau on Thursday 13 August 2026.
As reported by Inside Asian Gaming at the time, Genting Malaysia emerged as a surprise seventh bidder for a Macau gaming concession when a representative named Mrs Chen submitted the bid to the bidding committee in the final hours before the Macao SAR Government closed the submission period for bids under its re-tender process for new concessions. Mrs Chen, accompanied by three other people, submitted two boxes of documents before confirming to attending media that GMM was associated with Genting Malaysia and the person in charge was Genting Group Chairman Lim Kok Thay.
“Mr Lim Kok Thay wanted to come to Macau [to submit Genting’s bid] but he couldn’t come because of the pandemic,” she explained at the time.
Genting ultimately failed in its concession bid, with the Macao SAR Government announcing in November 2022 that the existing six concessionaires would be awarded new 10-year concessions.
Genting Malaysia said in Thursday’s filing that the members’ voluntary liquidation of GMM would not have any material impact on the net assets and earnings per share of the group for the financial year ending 31 December 2026.

title: Genting Malaysia winding down Macau unit GMM Ltd
body:
Casino operator Genting Malaysia Bhd is winding down GMM Ltd, the Macau-incorporated vehicle it used in an unsuccessful 2022 bid for a gaming concession in the city.

Genting Malaysia said in a Thursday filing that shareholders of GMM had resolved on Tuesday to dissolve the company. GMM has subsequently commenced a members’ voluntary liquidation.

The relevant documents were submitted to Macau’s Commerce and Movable Property Registry on Thursday, according to the filing.

Genting Malaysia described GMM as an “indirect wholly-owned dormant subsidiary” incorporated in Macau.

The parent said the voluntary liquidation would not have any material impact on the net assets and earnings per share of Genting Malaysia for the financial year ending December 31, 2026.

GMM was the vehicle used by Genting Malaysia to participate in Macau’s 2022 public tender for new gaming concessions. Its emergence as a seventh bidder created competition for the six concessions available under the city’s gaming regulatory framework.

GMM submitted its proposal in September 2022. The bid was initially admitted on a “conditional” basis by the Macau government committee overseeing the tender process. The submissions from the six incumbent operators were admitted for consideration without any attached conditions.

The GMM proposal was subsequently accepted for consideration “unconditionally” , meaning all seven bids were admitted to compete for the six available concessions.

Genting Malaysia ultimately failed to secure a concession . The Macau government in November 2022 selected proposals from the city’s six incumbent operators.

At the time, the government said those six proposals were considered the “most advantageous” for Macau. The new concessions took effect on January 1, 2023, and run for 10 years.

Genting Malaysia operates Resorts World Genting, Malaysia’s only casino complex, and has gaming operations in a number of other jurisdictions.

The Genting group had also sought entry to the Macau casino market during the liberalisation process conducted around the turn of the century, but was not selected on that occasion either.

title: Maybank cuts Genting Malaysia 2026 earnings forecast by 28% with possible net loss in Q2 on Middle East war, World Cup impact
body:
Maybank Investment Bank says it anticipates a weaker performance from Genting Malaysia Bhd when the casino operator releases its 2Q26 financial results next month, with historical negative seasonality to be further magnified by the impact of the Middle East war and diverted gaming spend during the World Cup.
This, said analyst Samuel Yin Shao Yang, has led Maybank to slash its FY26 earnings forecast by 28%, adding, “We do not discount the possibility that Genting Malaysia may report a 2Q26 core net loss.”
In a note previewing the company’s Q2 results, Yin said, “Traditionally, 2Q is a seasonally weak quarter post-Chinese New Year. Yet we understand from channel checks that 2Q26 will be an unusually weak one.
“First, we understand that high diesel prices caused by the Middle East War dented VIP and mass market gaming at RWG. Second, the Middle East War could have discouraged Middle Easterners and gamblers who transit there from gambling at Genting UK’s London VIP clubs.
“Third, the FIFA World Cup diverted gaming spend from [Malaysia’s] Resorts World Genting and Genting UK.”
Despite the negative short-term outlook, Maybank said it was only trimming its 2027 and 2028 forecasts by 4% each, mainly because it expects the headwinds to be temporary. It also sees rapidly improving contribution from Resorts World New York City (RWNYC) following the recent launch of table game operations and ongoing expansion works.
“Since deploying table games on 28 Apr, RWNYC table games weekly GGR has hit US$11.1 million (from US$4.9 million during opening week) which implies average daily GGR per table of US$6,539 – a whole US$1,000 above our forecast of US$5,500 as operations ramp up,” Yin wrote.
“Slot machines GGR have been cannibalized by 12% since opening week but table games attract a lower gaming tax rate of 30% versus 56% for slot machines. Thus, the GGR mix is net positive to Genting Malaysia.”
Maybank is now forecasting Genting Malaysia to generate revenue of MYR13.1 billion (US$3.20 billion) and EBITDA of MYR3.18 billion (US$778 million) in 2026, rising to MYR15.7 billion (US$3.84 billion) and MYR3.98 billion (US$974 million) in 2027 and then MYR17.4 billion (US$4.26 billion) and MYR4.34 billion (US$1.06 billion) in 2028.
Genting Malaysia is scheduled to release its 2Q26 results on 20 August.

title: Genting Malaysia may report loss in 2Q, analyst warns
body:
KUALA LUMPUR (July 30): Genting Malaysia Bhd (KL:GENM) may report a net loss in what could turn out to be an unusually weak second quarter for the casino-and-resort operator, an analyst flagged.
While April-June are seasonally weak months, the Iran war may have dented both premium and mass market gaming at its flagship resort in Genting Highlands, as well as discouraged Middle Easterners and transit gamblers from its London clubs, Maybank Investment Bank said.
The Fifa World Cup that began mid-June may also have diverted gaming spend, the research house said in a note ahead of its earnings report expected in the final days of August.
Shares of Genting Malaysia have declined close to 10% year-to-date and are approaching this year’s lows in March, as the Iran war dragged into the sixth month and widened in the Middle East. Oil prices have surged, raising the cost of transportation while dragging on travel demand.
Genting Malaysia has seven “buy” and seven “hold” calls among 14 research houses tracked by Bloomberg. The 12-month average target price stood at RM2.34 per share.
Maybank Investment cut its target price to RM2.82, after slashing its earnings forecast but kept its “buy” call on the stock. “We believe these headwinds could be temporary,” the research house said.
Further, table games at its New York City facility have performed better than expected as operations ramp up, resulting in higher gross gaming revenue for Genting Malaysia, the house noted.
By 2027, the entire US operations could account for more than one-third of Genting Malaysia’s operating earnings, an increase of 20 percentage-points from 2025, according to Maybank Investment’s estimates.
“It is this earnings growth that compels us to maintain our buy rating,” the house added.

title: Maybank slashes GEN Malaysia full-year earnings forecast by 28pct, fears 2Q core net loss
body:
Maybank Investment Bank Bhd has cut by 28 percent its full-year earnings forecast for global casino operator Genting Malaysia Bhd, citing “lower” gross gaming revenue (GGR) performance at the group’s Malaysian casino monopoly, Resorts World Genting, and at Genting Casinos United Kingdom Ltd.

Analyst Samuel Yin Shao Yang said in a Wednesday memo there was risk of a “core net loss” for the second quarter this year.

Previewing Genting Malaysia’s numbers for the three months to June 30, Maybank stated: “The second quarter is a seasonally weak quarter, post-Chinese New Year. Yet we understand from channel checks that second-quarter 2026 will be an unusually weak one.”

Mr Yin mentioned a number of factors. Referring to the conflict between the United States and Iran, which has affected fuel supplies that usually transit the Strait of Hormuz, he wrote: “First, we understand that high diesel prices caused by the Middle East war dented VIP and mass market gaming at Resorts World Genting.”

Second, the conflict “could have discouraged Middle Easterners and gamblers who transit there, from gambling” at Genting’s UK “London VIP clubs”.

He added: “Third, the FIFA World Cup – 11 June to 19 July 2026 – diverted gaming spend from Resorts World Genting and Genting’s UK” properties.”

Nonetheless, the institution said it was cutting the firm’s earnings forecast for 2027 and 2028 “by only 4 percent”, as it believes such headwinds “could be temporary”.

For the Genting Malaysia group’s downstate New York operation – Resorts World New York City – which switched to being a full-service casino earlier this year, “table games traction, lower slot machine tax rates, and expanding capacity underpins Genting Malaysia’s long-term growth,” Mr Yin said.

title: Genting Malaysia faces 2Q26 core loss despite New York gains: Maybank
author: Viviana Chan
body:
Genting Malaysia could report a core net loss in 2Q26 after the FIFA World Cup and the Middle East conflict weakened gaming activity in Malaysia and the UK, according to Maybank Investment Bank.
The brokerage cut its FY2026 core net profit forecast by 28 percent to MYR480 million ($119 million), from MYR662.7 million ($164 million). Its assumptions now point to a 5 percent decline in gross gaming revenue (GGR) at both Resorts World Genting and Genting UK, compared with previous forecasts of 2 percent growth and flat performance, respectively.
Maybank said the second quarter is normally seasonally weaker following Chinese New Year, but channel checks indicated that 2Q26 could be unusually soft.
Higher diesel prices linked to the Middle East conflict reportedly affected VIP and mass-market play at Resorts World Genting. The conflict may also have discouraged Middle Eastern customers and travelers transiting through the region from visiting Genting UK’s London VIP clubs.
The FIFA World Cup, held between June 11th and July 19th, also diverted gaming spending from the two operations, Maybank said.
The brokerage did not rule out a 2Q26 core net loss, compared with a MYR10.2 million ($2.5 million) core profit in the previous quarter.
However, Maybank cut its FY2027 and FY2028 profit forecasts by only 4 percent, saying the ‘negative catalysts are transient’. It expects core net profit to more than double to MYR975.2 million ($241 million) in 2027.
New York growth offsets near-term pressure
Maybank said the expansion of table gaming at Resorts World New York City was supporting Genting Malaysia’s longer-term earnings outlook.
Weekly table GGR increased from $4.9 million during the opening week to $11.1 million in the week ending July 19th. Daily GGR per table reached $6,539, exceeding Maybank’s forecast of $5,500.
Slot GGR has fallen by about 12 percent since tables were introduced on April 28th. However, Maybank said the changing revenue mix remained positive because table games are subject to a 30 percent gaming tax, compared with 56 percent for slots.
The reduction of the slot tax rate from 68 percent to 56 percent is expected to add about $120 million to annual group EBITDA.
Resorts World New York City added 1,400 slot machines on July 21st, bringing its total to about 3,900. It plans to add approximately 160 tables by the end of 2026 or early 2027.
Maybank expects Genting Malaysia’s US operations to contribute 36 percent of group EBITDA in 2027, up from 16 percent in 2025. It maintained its buy rating but lowered its target price.

title: Genting breaks ground on $5.5B Resorts World NYC Phase Two expansion plan
author: AGBrief Editorial
body:
Asia Gaming eBrief: Resorts World NYC breaks ground on $5.5B expansion
Genting has moved quickly from opening the doors to expanding the footprint. The group has started work on the $5.5 billion second phase of Resorts World New York City, which will add two hotel components, a 7,000-seat arena and new gaming and hospitality facilities. The groundbreaking comes less than three months after the Queens property became New York City’s first full commercial casino. Meanwhile, Morgan Stanley says Sands China’s higher gaming volumes have yet to produce consistent EBITDA share gains, as increased customer spending and operating costs continue to squeeze margins.
Genting Group began the second phase of its $5.5 billion Resorts World New York City expansion on July 22nd. Plans include two hotel additions providing 1,600 rooms, a 7,000-seat multipurpose arena, a central plaza and a new parking garage. The full development will add 2 million square feet of gaming, entertainment, dining, retail and convention space to the existing Queens property.

title: Genting breaks ground on Phase 2 of US$5.5 billion Resorts World New York City expansion
body:
Just days after opening a new gaming floor and adding 1,400 more slot machines, Genting’s Resorts World New York City (RWNYC) has officially broken ground on Phase 2 of its US$5.5 billion expansion.
The project follows the issuance late last year of one of three full casino licenses in downstate New York. With the other two – Bally’s Corp in the Bronx and Hard Rock International in Metropolitan Park – building from scratch, RWNYC is already enjoying first mover advantage as it gradually builds out its existing facility in Queens over the next five years. The property, which previously offered electronic gaming only, launched the state’s first gaming tables in April.
“In less than 3 months after opening our doors as the first casino in New York City’s history, we are already moving towards a day when the city will have a first-of-its-kind integrated resort,” said Tan Sri Lim Kok Thay, Executive Chairman of the Genting Group. “Not only are we keeping every commitment we made in our proposal to the state, but we are running well ahead of schedule in starting to build outside of our existing building.”
The Phase 2 expansion will include development of an additional 400-room hotel tower to add on to the current Hyatt Regency; the Kenny “The Jet” Sports and Media Complex; a 7,000 seat multi-purpose arena; 1,200 additional hotel rooms under the luxury Crockfords brand; the central plaza; and a state-of-the-art parking garage.
According to Genting, full expansion is projected to create 10,000 jobs, including an estimated 5,000 union construction jobs, and will add 2 million square feet of new gaming, entertainment, dining, retail and convention space to the existing one-million-square-foot property.
“The excitement around this project hasn’t stopped since the day we submitted our bid,” said Robert DeSalvio, President, Genting Americas East. “It carried us through our licensing process and through the first 12 weeks of operating New York City’s first live table games. Today, that same excitement is present as we break ground on Phase 2, which will bring new infrastructure, new parking and the next wave of hotel rooms that will support two million square feet of new gaming, entertainment, and hospitality space in the years ahead.”
RWNYC said it has since opening gaming tables on 28 April increased its tax and racing support payment by over 30% compared with the same period last year to more than US$170 million.
“With these numbers, Resorts World New York City is already the largest casino in the United States in terms of Gross Gaming Revenue,” the company stated.

title: Genting breaks ground on $5.5B Resorts World NYC Phase Two
author: Viviana Chan
body:
Genting Group broke ground on July 22nd on the second phase of its $5.5 billion Resorts World New York City expansion, less than three months after the Queens property opened as New York City’s first full commercial casino.
According to a company press release issued the same day, the second phase includes a new 400-room hotel tower adjoining the existing Hyatt Regency and 1,200 additional rooms under Genting’s luxury Crockfords brand. The additions will take the property’s planned hotel inventory to 2,000 rooms.
The project will also include a 7,000-seat multipurpose arena, a central plaza and a new parking garage.
The Kenny “The Jet” Sports and Media Complex will be relocated to the center of the resort campus and is scheduled to open three years earlier than initially pledged.
The full expansion will add 2 million square feet of gaming, entertainment, dining, retail and convention space to the existing 1-million-square-foot property. Genting expects the development to create 10,000 jobs, including about 5,000 union construction positions.
Genting Group executive chairman Lim Kok Thay said the company was beginning construction outside the property’s existing building ahead of its original timetable.
“In less than three months after opening our doors as the first casino in New York City’s history, we are already moving towards a day when the city will have a first-of-its-kind integrated resort,” Lim said.
Genting Americas East president Robert DeSalvio said interest in the project had remained strong since the company submitted its license bid.
“Today, that same excitement is present as we break ground on Phase Two, which will bring new infrastructure, new parking, and the next wave of hotel rooms that will support two million square feet of new gaming, entertainment, and hospitality space in the years ahead,” he said.
With only two gaming floors operating since the April 28th opening, Resorts World said the property paid $170 million in casino taxes and horse-racing support during its first 12 weeks. The amount was more than 30 percent higher than in the same period last year, when the property still operated as a video lottery terminal facility.
The groundbreaking comes after Lim said Resorts World New York City could become one of Genting Malaysia’s most successful investments and potentially match or surpass the performance of Singapore integrated resort Resorts World Sentosa.
Lim, who is also Genting Malaysia’s deputy chairman and chief executive, said the New York property’s performance had met expectations since opening. He cited the city’s population, per-capita income, financial sector and economic scale as supporting its long-term potential.
The property had operated as a video lottery terminal facility since 2011 before introducing more than 240 live tables on April 28th. Its phased expansion continued with the addition of 1,400 slot machines on July 21st.

title: Genting’s Fortune Seen Improving In 2H And 2027
body:
Genting Malaysia Bhd (GENM) is expected to deliver a stronger performance in the second half of 2026, supported by a recovery in visitor arrivals at Resorts World Genting (RWG) and improving earnings from its US casino operations, according to CIMB Research.

The research house maintained its “Neutral” rating on Malaysia’s gaming sector but reaffirmed GENM as its top pick, retaining a “Buy” call with a target price of RM2.50.

Resorts World Genting expected to rebound

CIMB noted that Malaysia’s tourism industry continued to perform strongly in early 2026, with international visitor arrivals rising 5.4% year-on-year to a record 10.6 million in the first quarter.

Chinese tourists remained the biggest growth driver, with arrivals increasing 25% year-on-year, supported by the Visit Malaysia Year campaign and the launch of 26 new scheduled and charter flight routes during the quarter.

Domestic tourism also remained resilient, with visitor numbers growing 7.2% while spending increased 15.8% year-on-year.

Despite the favourable tourism backdrop, RWG recorded a 4% year-on-year decline in visitor arrivals to 5.5 million during the first quarter, partly due to fewer school holidays following Malaysia’s return to a January academic calendar and lower theme park ticket sales after promotional pricing introduced last year.

CIMB expects RWG’s visitor numbers to return to year-on-year growth in the second half as domestic tourism continues to strengthen.

The research house added that concerns over higher international airfares are unlikely to significantly affect RWG, given that around 90% of its visitors are Malaysians and Singaporeans.

US casino operations gaining momentum

CIMB also expects GENM’s US operations to provide stronger earnings support over the coming quarters.
